title: PRAY TO THE LORD FOR ME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Pray to the Lord to take the frogs away from me and my people, and I will let your people go to offer sacrifices to the Lord."" - Exodus 8:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the first crack in Pharaoh's armour. The man who sneered "who is the Lord?" is now asking Moses to pray to that very Lord.

But look carefully at what he wants. Take the frogs away from me. He wants relief, not relationship. He wants the consequences removed, not his heart changed.

That is a temptation for all of us. In pain, we pray fervently for the pain to stop. There is nothing wrong with that — Scripture is full of such prayers. But if the only thing we ever want from God is relief, we may be treating Him as a service rather than a Saviour.

Notice also that Pharaoh makes a promise while under pressure. Promises made in a crisis have a poor survival rate. Ecclesiastes warns that it is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfil it (Eccl 5:5).

And notice Moses' willingness to pray for the man oppressing his people. Jesus told us to pray for those who persecute us (Mt 5:44). Moses was already doing it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I want God to change my circumstances or to change me?
2. Is there a promise I made to God under pressure that I have quietly abandoned?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, do not let me seek only relief when what I need is You. Change my heart, not just my situation. Amen.
